turns.en: When did it start? Is it there all the time, or does it come and go? Does anything make it better or worse?
turns.cy: Pryd ddechreuodd o? Ydy o yna drwy'r amser, 'ta ydy o'n dod ac yn mynd? Oes 'na rywbeth yn ei neud o'n well neu'n waeth?
chunks: Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
Ydy o yna drwy'r amser, 'ta ydy o'n dod ac yn mynd?
the alternative-question 'ta (§4), and Welsh must restate the whole verb in the second limb
Does anything make it better or worse?
Oes 'na rywbeth yn ei neud o'n well neu'n waeth?
English's 'anything' as subject relocates to an existential; the causative takes a resumptive ei

turns.en: About two weeks ago. It's there all the time, more or less.
turns.cy: Rhyw bythefnos yn ôl. Mae o yna drwy'r amser, fwy neu lai.
chunks: pythefnos is one word — Welsh counts fortnights
It's there all the time, more or less
Mae o yna drwy'r amser, fwy neu lai

turns.en: And at its worst, how bad - one to ten? Has it stopped you doing anything? Work, sleep, the stairs?
turns.cy: A phan mae o ar ei waetha, pa mor ddrwg — un i ddeg? Ydy o wedi'ch stopio chi rhag gneud rhywbeth? Gwaith, cysgu, y grisiau?
chunks: A phan mae o ar ei waetha
English's bare prepositional phrase needs a Welsh clause — 'when it is at its worst'
pa mor ddrwg — un i ddeg?
pa mor is obligatory before a Welsh adjective
Has it stopped you doing anything?
Ydy o wedi'ch stopio chi rhag gneud rhywbeth?
the blocking preposition rhag, which English does not express

turns.en: An eight at its worst. I've not been to work since Monday.
turns.cy: Wyth ar ei waetha. Dw i heb fod yn y gwaith ers dydd Llun.
chunks: I've not been to work since Monday
Dw i heb fod yn y gwaith ers dydd Llun
the heb-negative perfect; and present + ers for the duration

turns.en: That's really helpful. One more thing - have you ever had anything like this before?
turns.cy: Mae hynna'n help mawr. Un peth arall — ydach chi wedi cael rhywbeth fel hyn o'r blaen?
chunks: English's adjective relocates to a noun — 'a big help'
have you ever had anything like this before?
ydach chi wedi cael rhywbeth fel hyn o'r blaen?
'ever' erases into the perfect, and 'anything' → rhywbeth in the question (S9)

turns.en: Never like this, no. That's why I came, really.
turns.cy: Erioed fel hyn, naddo. Dyna pam ddois i, a deud y gwir.
chunks: the verb-echo answer system: a perfect question is answered naddo, never 'no'
Dyna pam ddois i, a deud y gwir
'really' here is the sentence-final hedge — it converges with 'actually', which is reception

turns.en: When did it start? Does anything make it better or worse?
turns.cy: Pryd ddechreuodd o? Oes 'na rywbeth yn ei neud o'n well neu'n waeth?
chunks: Does anything make it better or worse?
Oes 'na rywbeth yn ei neud o'n well neu'n waeth?

turns.en: Do you mean the pain or the dizziness? Because they started at different times.
turns.cy: Ydach chi'n meddwl y boen 'ta'r penysgafnder? Achos mi ddechreuon nhw ar wahanol adegau.
chunks: Do you mean the pain or the dizziness?
Ydach chi'n meddwl y boen 'ta'r penysgafnder?
Because they started at different times
Achos mi ddechreuon nhw ar wahanol adegau

turns.en: Good point - let's take them one at a time. The pain first. When did that begin?
turns.cy: Pwynt da — dewch i ni eu cymryd nhw un ar y tro. Y boen gynta. Pryd ddechreuodd honno?
chunks: let's take them one at a time
dewch i ni eu cymryd nhw un ar y tro
feminine honno, agreeing with poen — English's 'that' is genderless

turns.en: The pain came first, maybe a month ago. The dizziness is newer - a week or so.
turns.cy: Y boen ddaeth gynta, rhyw fis yn ôl ella. Mae'r penysgafnder yn fwy diweddar — rhyw wythnos.
chunks: the focus cleft: the subject fronts and the verb soft-mutates behind it
English's fronted 'maybe' lands clause-finally as ella
The dizziness is newer - a week or so
Mae'r penysgafnder yn fwy diweddar — rhyw wythnos
Welsh takes the periphrastic comparative here, where English takes the synthetic one

turns.en: That's a useful distinction. Has there been any weight loss, any fevers, night sweats?
turns.cy: Mae hynna'n wahaniaeth defnyddiol. Oes 'na fod colli pwysau, unrhyw dwymyn, chwysu yn y nos?
chunks: Has there been any weight loss, any fevers, night sweats?
Oes 'na fod colli pwysau, unrhyw dwymyn, chwysu yn y nos?
English's perfect existential relocates to a present one with a bod complement; 'any' → unrhyw in the free-choice list (S9)

turns.en: Now you mention it, my trousers are looser on me. I thought that was a good thing.
turns.cy: Rŵan dach chi'n sôn, mae fy nhrowsus i'n llacach amdana i. Ro'n i'n meddwl bod hynny'n beth da.
chunks: ⚠ line — English's object 'it' erases; sôn is intransitive in Welsh
my trousers are looser on me
mae fy nhrowsus i'n llacach amdana i
⚠ line — trowsus is singular in Welsh; the conjugated amdana i
I thought that was a good thing
Ro'n i'n meddwl bod hynny'n beth da

turns.en: When did it start? Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
turns.cy: Pryd ddechreuodd o? Ydy o yna drwy'r amser, 'ta ydy o'n dod ac yn mynd?
chunks: Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
Ydy o yna drwy'r amser, 'ta ydy o'n dod ac yn mynd?

turns.en: Hard to say, really. It sort of crept up on me. Months, maybe?
turns.cy: Anodd deud, a deud y gwir. Mi wnaeth o rywsut gripian i fyny arna i. Misoedd, ella?
chunks: Anodd deud, a deud y gwir
English's copula erases in the elliptical judgement
It sort of crept up on me
Mi wnaeth o rywsut gripian i fyny arna i
the conjugated arna i carries English's 'on me'

turns.en: Roughly is fine. Was it there at Christmas, say? Before the summer?
turns.cy: Mae bras yn iawn. Oedd o yna adeg y Nadolig, deudwch? Cyn yr haf?
chunks: a bare adverb cannot subject a Welsh clause — mae must be built under it
Was it there at Christmas, say?
Oedd o yna adeg y Nadolig, deudwch?
English's parenthetical 'say' relocates to the imperative deudwch

turns.en: It was there at Christmas, now you say it. Maybe before, even.
turns.cy: Roedd o yna adeg y Nadolig, rŵan dach chi'n deud. Cyn hynny hyd yn oed, ella.
chunks: Roedd o yna adeg y Nadolig
kept distinct from 'now you mention it' → rŵan dach chi'n sôn
Cyn hynny hyd yn oed, ella
Welsh puts hyd yn oed after what it scopes over, where English puts 'even' at the end

turns.en: That helps me more than you'd think. Let me ask a few more, then I'll take a proper look.
turns.cy: Mae hynna'n fy helpu i fwy nag y basach chi'n feddwl. Gadwch i mi ofyn chydig mwy, wedyn mi gymra i olwg iawn.
chunks: That helps me more than you'd think
Mae hynna'n fy helpu i fwy nag y basach chi'n feddwl
Let me ask a few more
Gadwch i mi ofyn chydig mwy
then I'll take a proper look
wedyn mi gymra i olwg iawn
sequential wedyn (S1); 'proper' → iawn, postposed as Welsh requires

turns.cy: Beth bynnag dach chi ei angen, doctor.
chunks: Beth bynnag dach chi ei angen, doctor
the bynnag free-relative; angen takes a possessive object ei
